item.title: Man United concede two penalties in three minutes in latest defensive horror show
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino saw his new Manchester United defence concede two penalties in the space of three minutes as the face Sporting in the Champions League in Lisbon. The hosts received the chance to open the scoring when Lisandro Martinez was ruled to have fouled winger Geny Catamo by catching him with an outstretched leg. Sporting v Man United LIVE: Latest Champions League score and updates If it appeared soft, justice was perhaps served when Senne Lammens saved a tame effort from Sporting striker Luis Suarez low down to his left. But in farcical scenes, Lammens then conceded another penalty just 75 seconds later when he crashed into Maximiliano Araujo in the box. Suarez took the second penalty and made no mistake to give Sporting the lead, as United conceded the opening goal for the seventh match in a row. Lammens conceded another penalty just 75 seconds after saving the first (PA) It was the first time United had conceded two penalties in the same Champions League match since 1998, while they have now conceded five in total in all competitions this season. United’s players were also left furious as Amad Diallo’s equaliser was disallowed for a foul in the build-up. Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled that Youri Tielemans had committed a foul on Goncalo Inacio when he slid to poke the ball through to Amad. The United winger saw his shot saved by Sporting goalkeeper Kaique Pereira but he followed in to head the ball into an empty net. The goal could not be reviewed because the referee had already given a foul (PA) However, because Marciniak had already blown his whistle to stop play following the challenge from Tielemans, VAR could not intervene. Tielemans did not appear to commit a foul and instead won the ball fairly against Inacio when he went to ground to play the ball through to Amad. Tielemans was also booked by Marciniak for protesting.

item.title: Zac Taylor looks back on Bengals disappointing loss at Washington
item.description: Of the Cincinnati Bengals ' three losses so far in 2026, the Nov. 23 loss to the Washington Commanders was really the one that got away. The Bengals (7-3) were competitive in all three losses to varying degrees, but at Washington , they led most of the night, recaptured the lead with under a minute to play and couldn't get one final stop after that in a 22-20 walk-off field goal win for the Commanders (4-5-1). Bengals Commanders Jason Williams Hey, Zac Taylor, Joe Burrow. What happened to running the ball? Cincinnati has a short week to prepare for their Nov. 29 home game against the New Orleans Saints (3-7), but spent most of his Nov. 25 news conference at Paycor Stadium revisiting key aspects of the costly loss to the Commanders. The status of the Bengals' run game Following the Bengals' Sunday Night Football win over AFC North rival Pittsburgh on Nov. 15, one Bengals' captain essentially chalked up the state of the Bengals' running game to: "When we're passing it like we are, why force a running game." That wasn't a bad way to think about the win over the Steelers, which the Bengals dominated. But at Northwest Stadium against Washington, Cincinnati amassed just 31 rushing yards. That sum flirted with the 23 yards they gained on the ground in the loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Oct. 4, which stands as the worst rushing game by the team under Taylor. The working theory within the Bengals' offense has a few prongs related to the run game, and one was conveyed by the Bengals' captain. Another prong is that the Bengals have passing plays that essentially function as running plays using dump-offs around the line of scrimmage. And maybe those plays develop in ways that are more advantageous for Cincinnati's backs, Chase Brown and Samaje Perine. The Bengals are going into Week 12, and Taylor seemed to say the Bengals are who they are when it comes to running the ball. With that could come difficulties in games like the one they lost as Washington. "I think 'Pitch' (offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher) said it best: 'We'll be whoever we need to be as the year goes on," Taylor said. "He said that in training camp and in the offseason. I still feel very strongly about that as the season goes." item.title: Matisse Thybulle Is the Lakers’ Secret Weapon
item.description: One of the biggest keys to the Lakers’ stupendous 15-3 start has been defensive standout Matisse Thybulle . The Lakers acquired Thybulle over last offseason on a $3.3 million deal. So far, he has been worth every penny. Leading the Way for the Lakers’ Defense Eighteen games in, the Lakers are hovering near the top 10 in defensive rating, thanks in part to them ranking first in steals per game and second in blocks . A large part of their success on that end of the floor is Thybulle’s defensive prowess. Against the Charlotte Hornets on Nov. 17, Thybulle’s defense helped L.A. win in overtime. With 11.5 seconds left in the game, the Lakers led 117-114. Hornets guard Royce O’Neale tried to inbound the ball when Thybulle flew in for a deflection that sealed the victory. Matisse in the clutch to seal it! The #Lakers are riding the wave pic.twitter.com/Xqc1VpCUzH — Spectrum SportsNet (@SpectrumSN) November 18, 2026 On a night when Quentin Grimes exploded for 47 points, Thybulle was the unsung hero. Making big defensive plays is nothing new for the former Naismith Defensive Player of the Year. He ranks second in steals per game in the NBA (among those who have played at least five games), and boasts the most games with at least two steals and one block. He is on pace to be the first Laker ever to average two steals and a block for a season. Matisse Thybulle already has 11 games with 2+ steals and a block this season, while no other NBA player has more than 6. pic.twitter.com/n7I1QQ4KvG — Screwball NBA (@ScrewballNBA) November 24, 2026 Thybulle’s defensive tendencies impressed his teammates before the season even started. Back in training camp, rookie Cameron Carr named Matisse as the player who stood out the most, touting his defense as “ridiculous.” With each game, Thybulle has continued to amaze. “Honestly, he has those instincts of getting to the ball; it’s like ‘What, how did he get there?’” said teammate Collin Sexton . “So I think just being out there with him, you have to communicate with him; sometimes he communicates with you as well, like, ‘I got it. I’m gonna get the steal,’ and he goes out there and does it. He’s one of those players that has great instincts, but also can read the game before it happens on the defensive side, so it’s cool to be out there.” Thybulle Is Growing His Game Just as a coach gives star players the green light offensively, the same can be true for the defensive end. item.title: WWE Survivor Series 2026 predictions: Will The Rock and Cody Rhodes turn WrestleMania season upside down?
item.description: Survivor Series: WarGames , WWE's final "Big Four" premium live event of 2026, goes down this weekend in Houston. Although the event has shifted in recent years to be headlined by "the match beyond," this year's edition will also feature a traditional five-on-five Survivor Series match between Team USA and Team Mexico. In addition to the in-ring action, WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson will make an appearance on the show, leaving the wrestling world buzzing about a potential return to the ring for "The Final Boss." With so much to dissect heading into Survivor Series: WarGames, the Uncrowned Horsemen — Kel Dansby, Robert Jackman, Drake Riggs and Anthony Sulla-Heffinger — have gathered to break down all the angles and make predictions for the event. Let's ride! 1. What do you expect from The Rock's appearance this weekend? In your ideal world, what comes from his return? Riggs: It's really difficult to say. Honestly, after seeing John Cena break the fourth wall into a million pieces recently, I could totally see Rock returning literally just to say something nice in a reflective, nothing-promo about his WWE career. Given how Saturday's appearance has been advertised, that outcome feels likely — at a minimum. Whether he returns a second time on the show is another question. Ideally, I think he should, and it should come after 946 beats the Bloodline, with Roman Reigns taking the pin. As the only man you can put ahead of Reigns "at the table," Rock should walk out to feign being supportive, but instead be disappointed that his family (Reigns specifically) failed in this "war" and failed the family as a whole. He hits Reigns with a Rock Bottom as the rest of the crew stares in disbelief, but refuses to do anything because, again, Rock is the only guy above Reigns. That sets up their eventual "SaudiMania" dream match that's been wanted for years — ideally, again, with Reigns dropping the title to Oba Femi before then. Rock vs. Reigns doesn't need the title. Just put the "Ufa Lafa," as LA Knight once said, on the line and call it good. This is too easy, which is why WWE won't do it, sadly. Jackman: I'm betting on The Rock springing a Hall of Fame surprise on John Cena. The WWE Hall of Fame ceremony has lacked that star power over the past few years and immortalizing the 17-time champion is the perfect way to fix that. item.title: Aaron Rodgers Claims He Found Out About Steelers Benching from Teammate
item.description: Aaron Rodgers on Nov. 22, 2026. Credit: Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty NEED TO KNOW Aaron Rodgers says he learned of his sudden benching from the Pittsburgh Steelers from a teammate He said Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth broke the news on a phone call Nov. 24, the same night the team shared the news widely Rodgers recalled the call while breaking his silence and sharing that his time with the Steelers is over on The Pat McAfee Show on Nov. 25 Fans learned Aaron Rodgers is no longer the Pittsburgh Steelers’ starting quarterback on social media. He says he got the news from a teammate. The 42-year-old quarterback recalled the moment he learned he would be inactive for the Steelers’ next game during a surprise appearance Wednesday, Nov. 25 on The Pat McAfee Show . Rodgers, who previously said he would retire at the end of the season , claimed he learned the news of his status from tight end Pat Freiermuth before leveling a handful of accusations at head coach Mike McCarthy. “I found out that I was going to be inactive on a phone call last night with Pat Freiermuth,” the NFL star told host Pat McAfee and co-host A.J. Hawk on Wednesday’s program. Head coach Mike McCarthy talks with Aaron Rodgers in September 2026 Credit: Joe Sargent/Getty “I was talking to Muth and a couple of the guys, and he said, ‘I can’t believe they’re doing this.’ And I said, ‘Doing what?’ I didn’t know,” Rodgers continued. “And he told me, and obviously there had been a lot of things in motion at that point.” The four-time NFL MVP said that his removal from the starting position never came up in conversation with McCarthy — who coached Rodgers for more than a decade in Green Bay — prior to the benching. “I didn’t hear from Mike,” Rodgers claimed, adding the two last spoke around 6 p.m. on Tuesday, Nov. 24. “Still haven’t heard from people over there,” Rodgers said, adding his agents “obviously talked with” Steelers general manager Omar Khan. “Yeah, the way it was released last night, and like trying to get out and ahead, like there was some benching going on… Mike and I talked for a long time the last few days, that word never even came up,” Rodgers said. On Wednesday in the Steelers’ locker room, Freiermuth said he “was just checking in on a close friend” when asked about the call with Rodgers. The Steelers did not immediately return PEOPLE’s request for comment. The Steelers announced the quarterback change late Tuesday night. item.title: Aaron Rodgers shows Fernando Mendoza love during scorched earth Steelers rant
item.description: Aaron Rodgers just had one of the most memorable interviews in recent sports history on the “Pat McAfee Show” Wednesday. One day after news broke that he would not be starting for the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday, Rodgers went scorched earth on Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, including (but not limited to) revealing that McCarthy was snoring during team meetings this past week. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers gestures at a news conference after an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles in Philadelphia, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/Chris Szagola The 42-year-old quarterback ( who was released by the Steelers shortly after the interview concluded) did not mince words about his former head coach and franchise. But the interview was not all negative. Rodgers took a moment to show Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza some love. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) speaks during a press conference after an NFL football game in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/David Becker Rodgers was talking about the play calling he has seen that he has liked around the league and said, “And I’ll tell you: Hey, the kid Mendoza, man. He was running around, making some plays in the scramble.” Rodgers is one of the greatest quarterbacks in NFL history and knows what good play at the position looks like. Therefore, his positive endorsement of Mendoza’s performance speaks volumes, even if it has not amounted to a win for Las Vegas. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) passes against the Seattle Seahawks during an NFL football game in Las Vegas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. item.title: Atlanta boosts left-handed pitching depth with latest signing
item.description: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Atlanta boosts left-handed pitching depth with latest signing appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Braves are continuing to add options to their pitching staff as they prepare for the 2027 season. Their latest move brings another left-handed arm into the organization , giving Atlanta additional depth ahead of Spring Training. According to New York Post reporter Jon Heyman, Atlanta has agreed to a minor-league contract signing left-hander Charlie Barnes. The 31-year-old will also receive an invitation to Major League Spring Training. Barnes has previously appeared in the majors with the Minnesota Twins, Chicago Cubs, and Los Angeles Dodgers. Barnes made five MLB appearances during the 2026 campaign, including one with Chicago and four with Los Angeles. He struggled in those outings, allowing 11 runs, 10 of them earned, on 17 hits and seven walks across 13 innings. He also recorded six strikeouts. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Most of his work came in the minors. Barnes posted a 3.48 ERA with 80 strikeouts and 34 walks over 82 2/3 innings between the Triple-A affiliates of the Cubs and Dodgers. He brings a five-pitch mix that includes a four-seam fastball, sinker, slider, changeup, and sweeper. The signing adds another left-handed pitcher to Atlanta’s organizational depth. The Braves have also retained Joey Wentz and Dylan Lee through contract tenders for 2027. They recently added left-hander Mitchell Parker after claiming him off waivers from the Washington Nationals. Barnes will now have an opportunity to compete for a spot during Spring Training. However, his minor-league contract means he will likely need to prove himself before earning a place on Atlanta’s major-league roster. The move drew reactions from fans online. One said that the signing was “Game changing,” while another declared, “World Series confirmed.”

item.title: Chelsea called upon to sign Virgil van Dijk amid Liverpool contract uncertainty
item.description: Virgil van Dijk's Liverpool contract is set to expire after this season -Credit:Michael Regan, Getty Images Jamie Redknapp has called on Chelsea to pursue Virgil van Dijk, asserting that the Liverpool defender still has at least two more years at the highest level, with the Anfield club deliberating over whether to hand him a contract extension. This leaves the Dutchman, who joined the Reds back in 2018, potentially seeking a new club when the summer arrives. His move to Merseyside coincided with Liverpool re-emerging as a trophy-winning powerhouse, and he has remained their defensive cornerstone for nearly a decade. Chelsea have recently overhauled their recruitment strategy, shifting away from targeting young talent — Xabi Alonso has instead looked to bring seasoned professionals into the fold, securing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson during the summer transfer window. Florian Wirtz on Liverpool struggles after record transfer and impact of Jürgen Klopp Pep Guardiola on Italy job talks with Paolo Maldini and 'next step' in career -Credit:Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images Redknapp is hopeful that Van Dijk will commit his future to Anfield, but should the Dutchman seek a fresh challenge, the analyst believes Chelsea should waste no time in extending his Premier League career by bringing him to Stamford Bridge. He told Sky Vegas , via The Mirror : "I don't know for sure, he might end up staying. I hope he does. They should try and get Virgil van Dijk in the summer. That's what I'd do. Just someone there, you're not going to get five years out of him, but I still think he's got two years at the top. "I think he'd be a great signing. He might want to go to the MLS. He might want to go somewhere. But he might fancy London. And if he doesn't sign a new contract at Liverpool, that's who they should try and sign." Redknapp pointed to how Thiago Silva, who didn't join Chelsea until he was 35, proved to be a massively influential figure in their backline despite his advancing years. The Brazilian would ultimately claim a UEFA Champions League title with the Blues. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Van Dijk acknowledged earlier this week that he himself remains uncertain about his own future, yet still believes he has plenty to contribute at the highest level. He said: "The main thing for me is that I feel good, and I'm looking after myself, and I still have many more years, in my opinion. Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see. At this moment of time, if anyone says that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either." The Dutchman also added: "If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer."

item.title: Daniel Dubois vs Joseph Parker set to deliver ‘blockbuster beginning to 2027’
item.description: The heavyweight division continues to be involved in many boxing conversations, with Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua edging closer. In addition, the current WBO champion Daniel Dubois is arguably the most in-form in the division after his two big wins over Fabio Wardley. Queensberry Promotions have now announced Daniel Dubois vs Joseph Parker . Daniel Dubois vs Joseph Parker set for new year showdown Daniel Dubois vs Joseph Parker (36-4, 24 KOs) was originally slated for February 2025, when Dubois, the then IBF champion, had to withdraw in fight week due to illness. Parker then stepped up to face late replacement Martin Bakole, whom he stopped in the second round. With that win over Bakole, Parker retained his WBO interim title. The Kiwi-Samoan then faced Fabio Wardley and was stopped in dramatic fashion in the eleventh round. Parker was then hit by a huge double blow after the fight; firstly, it was revealed he had failed a UKAD test for cocaine, which was later ruled Parker’s nutritionist was the reason that traces were found. Secondly, Wardley was upgraded to the full champion after Usyk vacated his WBO belt. The 34-year-old should be applauded for taking this opportunity for his first fight back. Dubois (24-3, 23 KOs) has recorded brilliant wins against Wardley x2 and Anthony Joshua among others. He fell short against Oleksandr Usyk on two occasions, and lost to Joe Joyce earlier in his career, but Dubois has improved immensely as he gets older. His wins over Jarrell Miller and Filip Hrgovic were also inspired. He has shown a willingness to face the best, and that has to be congratulated. His jab is like a power punch, and his right hand carries huge power. This is a huge fight for both, for very different reasons. Daniel Dubois vs Joseph Parker Daniel Dubois will defend his WBO title against Joseph Parker on Saturday, January 30, 2027, at Co-op Live, Manchester, live on DAZN. Parker won the WBO title in 2016 and has a strong resume, recording wins against Deontay Wilder, Zhilei Zhang, Martin Bakole and Derek Chisora twice. Setting the scene for this heavyweight dust-up, Queensberry founder Frank Warren said: “This heavyweight showdown will deliver a blockbuster beginning to 2027. item.description: Romania v Netherlands: Round of 16 - UEFA EURO 2024 - Getty Images Sport Watford have appointed former Romania boss Edward Iordanescu as their new head coach, just days after sacking Alessio Dionisi following a 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United. The 48-year-old becomes the 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over in 2012, and inherits a side sitting just three points above the Championship relegation zone after a dismal start. Iordanescu 'very confident' Iordanescu replaces Dionisi, who was dismissed on Sunday after only five months in charge following seven defeats in Watford's last 10 league games, culminating in Saturday's 4-0 loss at Sheffield United. "I am very proud and happy to be at this football club," the new head coach told the club's official website. He added: "I can see the team is in a difficult moment but I have already watched many of the games over the last few days and I'm very confident about the future." Sixth new boss in 18 months The Romanian is Watford's 25th manager since the Pozzo family took over in 2012, and their sixth new boss in less than 18 months, according to BBC Sport . He will be joined by backroom staff Alexandru Radu, Grzegorz Mokry and Michele Iannucci. Iordanescu was set to watch Wednesday's Championship clash with Blackburn Rovers from the stands, with former Watford defender Adrian Mariappa overseeing the game alongside Paul Furlong and Lloyd Doyley. Heading into that match, the Hornets had won only four of their 16 games and taken just one point from a possible 24 on the road. Trophy-winning CV The Watford job is Iordanescu's first since he left Legia Warsaw in October 2025, having won the Polish Super Cup during his spell in Poland. He previously guided CFR Cluj to the Romanian title and two domestic cups, and also managed CSKA Sofia and Steaua Bucharest. He spent two and a half years in charge of Romania, leading them to the last 16 of Euro 2024, where they were beaten 3-0 by the Netherlands. He is the son of Anghel Iordanescu, who took Romania to the quarter-finals of the 1994 World Cup. Stability the target at Watford Iordanescu's first task will be to steer Watford away from danger, starting at Derby on Saturday. He will also hope to bring stability to a club who had already appointed 12 permanent head coaches since the end of the 2020-21 season prior to his arrival.

The league announced Wednesday it is assembling a group of major global investors to help mobilize around $11 billion toward the development and renovation of basketball arenas and surrounding sports and entertainment districts across the continent. The initiative is designed to support the NBA and FIBA’s planned launch of a new professional league in Europe in fall 2027, giving prospective clubs and ownership groups access to long-term capital and the NBA’s expertise in arena development. The NBA wants to help develop modern venues that could become year-round destinations, with projects potentially including housing, restaurants, retail, offices and public spaces. item.title: Wiaan Mulder creates Test history, becomes first player to score triple ton and take seven-wicket haul
item.description: South Africa all-rounder Wiaan Mulder added another remarkable chapter to his Test career, achieving a rare double that had never been accomplished in the history of the longest format. The 28-year-old became the first player to score a triple century and claim a seven-wicket haul during his Test career, producing the historic feat in the second Test against Bangladesh at Centurion. Mulder's exceptional performance with the ball helped South Africa secure a commanding victory by an innings and 219 runs, completing a 2-0 series whitewash against Bangladesh. The achievement brought together two outstanding performances from the all-rounder, who had previously smashed an unbeaten 367 against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo in July 2025 before delivering a career-best bowling display against Bangladesh. From historic triple century to seven-wicket haul Mulder had scripted history during the second Test against Zimbabwe in Bulawayo on July 7, 2025, when he scored an unbeaten 367 on his Test captaincy debut. He reached the triple-century mark in just 297 deliveries, producing one of the finest innings by a South African batter in Test cricket. The Proteas eventually registered an innings-and-236-run victory. Nearly a year later, Mulder added another historic achievement to his name, this time with the ball against Bangladesh. The all-rounder returned sensational figures of 7/31 in the second innings, helping South Africa bowl out Bangladesh and seal a comprehensive victory. Mulder registers South Africa's best bowling figures against Bangladesh Mulder's 7/31 became the best bowling figures by a South African in a Test innings against Bangladesh. He surpassed Keshav Maharaj's previous record of 7/32, recorded in Durban in 2022. Maharaj had also claimed 7/40 in Gqeberha during the same year. Mulder's performance was also the second-best bowling return in a Test innings at Centurion. Kyle Abbott continues to hold the venue record with figures of 7/29 against Pakistan in 2013. Joins elite list of players with century and seven-wicket haul The exclusive list features some of the greatest all-rounders in cricket history, including: Jack Gregory (Australia) against England in Melbourne, 1920. Ian Botham (England) against Pakistan at Lord's, 1978. Ian Botham (England) against India at Mumbai, 1980. Ravichandran Ashwin (India) against West Indies at North Sound, 2016. Naseer Khan Maroofkhil (Afghanistan) against Zimbabwe in Sharjah, 2026. Wiaan Mulder (South Africa) against Bangladesh at Centurion. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
